 Judi Dench in a campaign for Sobell House Hospice (Image: Sobell House Hospice)

 It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald.
 UK acting legend Judi Dench has made a 'heartbreaking' health update.
 The iconic 91-year-old actress has had a storied career across stage and screen picking up Academy, Tony, Golden Globe and British Academy awards.
 Audiences know her as James Bond's boss M - a role she played in 7 films with Daniel Craig and Pierce Brosnan - as well as other movies such as Shakespeare in Love and Philomena.
 READ MORE: Boris Johnson, 62, in 'saving' career move away from the UK 
 Dame Judi is also a consistent stage actress, having worked on numerous plays for the National Theatre Company and the Royal Shakespeare Company.
 Dame Judi Dench (Image: Ian West/PA) 
 She has a number of links to Oxfordshire including having performed at the city Playhouse in the 1960s and has shown support for a number of the county's charities including appearing in campaigns for Sobell House Hospice.
 In addition, in 2000 she received an honorary Doctor of Letters degree from Oxford University.
 In recent years she has spoken out about her health problems and now she has told BBC Radio 4's Today programme that she is unable to perform on stage or read.
 Dame Judi Dench in a campaign for Sobell House Hospice (Image: Sobell House Hospice) 
 She was diagnosed with age-related macular degeneration in 2012, a condition that impacts vision, and her sight has deteriorated since.
 "I have to put up with it," Dame Judi said, "my ma had it too".
 READ MORE: Family-run Oxford hotel listed for £2.5m sale as owners release statement 
 She added: "I mean, I can't be on stage, I can't do a play anymore, can't do a film anymore. I can't read anymore."
 Her admission comes as she is releasing a memoir, written with her friend Brendan O’Hea.
 Fans of the acclaimed actress were quick to react with some commenting that it would be amazing if the BBC could do a documentary on the condition.
 Another said: "Heartbreaking for her. MD is such a torture, when you love the world. Courage, Dame Judi."
